cases.name: item-setext-rule-disagreement
cases.note: CommonMark and TypeScript read an item heading; Rust reads a paragraph and rule. File folding refuses before mutation.

cases.name: item-setext-trailing-nbsp
cases.note: marked's trim also removes a no-break space.

cases.name: item-setext-trailing-tab
cases.note: Both readers keep the item's tab in the heading, and both writers drop it.

cases.name: item-setext-lt-text
cases.note: marked keeps HTML-shaped lines out of a heading, and `<3` is not one.

cases.name: item-setext-lt-before-divider
cases.note: The underline makes the heading, and the next line is a paragraph, not a table divider.

cases.name: item-setext-open-tag-start
cases.note: marked reads no block HTML or tag in `<a`, so it is heading text. The strict proof treats `<a` as a tag, so only a settle with the file keeps these bytes.

cases.name: item-setext-close-tag-start
cases.note: marked reads no block HTML or tag in `</a`, so it is heading text. The strict proof treats `</a` as a tag, so only a settle with the file keeps these bytes.

cases.name: item-setext-after-hash-line
cases.note: The desktop keeps `#tag` as text and reads `a` as the heading. Rust reads the whole item as text.

cases.name: item-setext-two-lines
cases.note: marked reads one heading over both lines, which both writers spell as a heading and then a paragraph, so Rust refuses it.

cases.name: item-ordered-non-one
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 reads the blank-separated source and projection as an ordered child starting at 2.

cases.name: item-empty-bullet
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 reads the blank-separated source and projection as an empty bullet child.

cases.name: item-empty-ordered
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 reads the blank-separated source and projection as an empty ordered child.

cases.name: item-ordered-non-one-tight
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 and both readers keep the non-one ordered continuation as paragraph text.

cases.name: item-empty-bullet-tight
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 and both readers read the dash as an item setext underline.

cases.name: item-empty-ordered-tight
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 and both readers keep the empty ordered continuation as paragraph text.

cases.name: item-empty-whitespace-markers
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 reads whitespace-only bullet and ordered markers as empty child lists when separated from the preceding paragraph.

cases.name: item-math-table-before-ordered
cases.note: CommonMark 0.31.2 reads math and GFM table syntax as separate paragraphs. Ordered children remain separate after each. Rust keeps math as literal text; TypeScript reads a math block.

cases.name: fold-bare-bullet

cases.name: fold-bare-ordered

cases.name: fold-quote-bare-bullet

cases.name: literal-backtick-ordinal

cases.name: root-indented-space-line
cases.note: marked keeps the two spaces past the indent of a whitespace line inside the block.

cases.name: root-indented-quoted-list-tab
cases.note: The indented block's quote markers and tab are its text, so list tab normalization leaves them alone.

cases.name: root-space-tab-code
cases.note: marked strips the two spaces and keeps the tab; CommonMark 0.31.2 strips both.

cases.name: quote-lazy-indented-line
cases.note: marked continues the quoted paragraph with the indented line, as CommonMark 0.31.2 does. Rust reads a quote and then indented code, so it refuses.

- x
	```ts

	```
- Item three
cases.canonical:

- x
  ```ts

  ```

rules: Blank lines contain only spaces or tabs. Same-kind siblings across blanks form one loose list. An indented line after a blank starts another item paragraph; a nonblank unindented line can lazily continue the current paragraph. Children must reach their parent's marker content column. Task checkboxes are content after a two-column bullet marker. Refusals for ambiguous lines apply inside list bodies; root prose, rules and code remain accepted. Each projector output must be accepted unchanged by its projected reader. Ordered output is capped at nine digits. Letter and Roman prefixes are prose. Thematic breaks take precedence over list markers.
